newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - April 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - April 25.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Supreme Court is expected to reverse its earlier decision banning the signature campaign of the People's Initiative for Reforms, Modernisation and Action to extend the term of President Fidel Ramos, sources in the Supreme Court and the Senate say. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)
- The House of Representatives approve on second reading a joint resolution seeking to defer the barangay elections in May to coincide with next year's presidential elections. (PHILIPPINE STAR)
- President Fidel Ramos asks the Bureaus of Customs and Internal Revenues to weed out scalawags in their ranks. (MANILA STANDARD)
- The Philippine negotiating panel is asking communist rebels to accept the country's sovereignty before resuming their peace talks, the government say. (PHILIPINE JOURNAL)
- Four groups are vying to buy into the financially troubled Monte de Piedad Savings and Mortgage Bank, a Central Bank official says. (ALL PAPERS)
- The Department of Finance and the Bureau of Customs vow to step up regulatory reforms to stop smugglers from using duty-free shops inside special economic zones. (BUSINESS DAILY)
- Senate ways and means committee chairman Juan Ponce Enrile says the House version of the income tax bill is "simply unacceptable". (BUSINESSWORLD)

- JG Summit Holdings Inc says it is expected to open by October the Philippines' largest cement plant in the country, which will contribute to the projected 15 percent growth in earnings this year, JG chairman John Gokongwei says. (MANILA TIMES)
